hook.text: After five winning trades, you feel like you've cracked the code. You haven't. You've been lucky—and that's dangerous.

buildup.text: Overconfidence makes traders overestimate their skill and underestimate randomness in their results.

discovery.text: Studies show overconfident traders trade 65% more often and earn significantly lower returns than cautious ones.

twist.text: Early success is the most dangerous thing in trading. It teaches bad habits that the market later punishes.

climax.text: Keeping a trading journal that tracks reasoning—not just results—reveals when luck is masquerading as skill.

punchline.text: Luck visits. Skill stays. Know the difference.

quiz.question: Why is overconfidence dangerous in trading?
options: It leads to excess trading and underestimating risk
